newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call range-bound, seen weakening on inflows.
newsitem.headline: Indian call range-bound, seen weakening on inflows.

text.p: Indian call money opened steady at 6.75-7.50 percent on Friday, dealers said.
"Primay dealers have sold the newly auctioned 12.14 percent 2000 bond -- this may ease the pressure on call," said a dealer.
"The rates are likely to come down on good inflows and less demand," a dealer said.
"The Reserve Bank of India (RBI)'s intervention in the foreign exchange market and repayment of the last repo will add over 30 billion rupees to the liquidity," said a bank dealer.
This may take the call money rates to 5.0 percent, he added.
The securities market will remain stable and the prices will start picking up, as the call rates touch 5.0 percent levels, dealers said.
